_comment: Party-menu mon-icon animation schedule, banked for the future engine wiring rung (docs/party-menu-notes.md). Source: reference/pokeemerald/src/pokemon_icon.c + src/party_menu.c, cross-checked against dense stride-1 oracle captures of battle1-turn15-dense.json ticks 20064-20260.

mechanism.bitmapFrames: Each icon sprite is 32x32, backed by a 32x64 icon.png (2 stacked 32x32 bitmap frames: top=frame0, bottom=frame1). UpdateMonIconFrame (pokemon_icon.c:1230) alternates the OAM tile data between the two frames once sprite->animDelayCounter reaches 0.
mechanism.speedTable: 5 anim scripts (pokemon_icon.c sAnim_0..sAnim_4), each just frame0<->frame1 at a fixed per-frame delay: animNum 0=6 ticks/frame (fastest), 1=8, 2=14, 3=22, 4=29-but-both-entries-are-frame0 (frozen, no visible change).
mechanism.speedSelection: In the party menu specifically, UpdatePartyMonHPBar -> UpdateHPBar (party_menu.c:3951) calls SetPartyHPBarSprite(spriteId, animNum) where animNum = 0/1/2/3/4 for HP_BAR_FULL/GREEN/YELLOW/RED/(fainted-or-egg default) - i.e. the icon's bounce SPEED is driven by its own mon's current HP-bar color, not a global clock. Each icon sprite carries its own animDelayCounter/animCmdIndex - independent per icon, not synced.
mechanism.selectedBounce: AnimatePartySlot(slot, animNum 0/1 select-state) -> AnimateSelectedPartyIcon (party_menu.c:3978): the DESELECTED icon just runs SpriteCB_UpdatePartyMonIcon (plain frame flip in place). The SELECTED icon runs SpriteCB_BouncePartyMonIcon instead, which ALSO offsets sprite->y2 by -3 or +1 (alternating) every time UpdateMonIconFrame reports a frame advance - i.e. the cursor's own icon additionally hops vertically ~4px in sync with its frame flips. NOT independently re-derived to the pixel level this session (see docs/party-menu-notes.md open item) - the two composite targets where a selected icon is on screen (cursor-on-MAGBY, submenu) were pixel-harvested whole rather than decomposed for this reason.

ONIX.note: empirically static: dense stride-1 oracle capture over ticks 20070-20191 (121 ticks, >4x the nominal 29-tick sAnim_4 period) shows ZERO pixel change in ONIX's panel/icon region. sAnim_4's own frame table has both entries pointing at frame0 (no visible bitmap change expected), but source also implies a y2 vertical hop should still fire on the SELECTED icon (cursor starts on ONIX) every 29 ticks even with an unchanged bitmap - not observed. Open item: why the selected-icon y2 hop doesn't show for a fainted mon (plausible: a fainted-mon code path skips AnimateSelectedPartyIcon/uses a different callback entirely - not source-confirmed this session).

MAGBY.note: verified: reference-extracted frame0/frame1 bitmap+palette matches oracle pixels almost exactly at anchor (84,2) - diff 2px (frame0, tick 20070) / 8px (frame1, tick 20076) out of ~300-400 opaque pixels, residual not chased to root cause. Once selected (cursor moves here, tick >=~20205), the bounce y2 hop applies - not decomposed, see selectedBounce above.

BAYLEEF.note: verified: diff 17px (frame0, tick 20070) / 22px (frame1, tick 20076) out of ~300-400 opaque pixels, confined to a 3x6px block at screen (105-107,49-54) - a corner of the icon's own bottom-right; not resolved to root cause this session (candidate: a text/HP-bar glyph legitimately drawing over that exact corner at a higher priority, or a compiled-palette index-0 remap quirk specific to this icon.png). Never selected in this turn's script (cursor never reaches BAYLEEF), so no bounce-hop variant needed.

empiricalCombinedStateTable.note: Full stride-1 dense capture (ticks 20064-20260) of the observed combined-screen sha256 sequence is not reproduced here in full (see docs/party-menu-notes.md §3 for the summary) - both MAGBY and BAYLEEF's independent frame0/frame1 flips combine into up to 4 distinct observable screen states during the settled 'cursor on ONIX' plateau; hold durations vary tick-to-tick (measured 1-8 ticks between combined-state changes) rather than the clean 6/6 the sAnim_0 source constant alone would predict for two perfectly-independent period-12 signals - open item, not resolved to a precise interleaving model this session.
